why: The page that carries this branch's most important behavioural history. Before role synthesis it produced 19 findings, 16 of them phantom nested-cards from the class-name regex matching `card-title`. After deriving roles from facts it produces 3. Pinning it means that regression cannot come back unnoticed. Snapshotted with its stylesheet; origin jang-personal-site/reference-html/index.html, copied 2026-08-28, finding count verified identical to the source at snapshot time.

verdicts.reason: FIXED (PR-FU3-r2 A7). The original 'tp' call took the finding's own words ('textless') at face value; read against the element, the 16 siblings are `<a class="card">` Magazine-issue links, each carrying a title, a description, an issue badge and an 'Open →' label in nested children — an ordinary content-card grid, never a textless illustration. The rule compared a structure fact's OWN line against every text fact's line; the cards' copy sits on the nested title/desc/badge/link lines, never the `<a>`'s own line, so every card read as textless. A real persona page's `<dl>` of five metric cards hit the identical shape (a `dt`/`dd` pair nested inside each card `div`) and is what surfaced the bug. Fixed by checking the structure's hierarchical `nodeRef` for a text-fact descendant instead of line equality (src/core/tell-rules-motion.ts). This row is now a regression tripwire: if it fires again, the descendant-text check has regressed to line-equality.
verdicts.message: 16 rounded, textless sibling shapes under html > body > div.grid[1] — an illustration assembled from primitives
